title: Ohm's law: why doubling the voltage doubles the current
examples: What is the unit of resistance?

explain.say: Imagine a torch with one battery, then two. With two, it shines brighter. Why? More voltage pushes more current through the bulb. Voltage means the push from the battery; current means the flow of charge. Let us measure it.

draw.text: Ohm's law: why doubling the voltage doubles the current

explain.say: Here is a graph for a resistor, a part that limits current. See the yellow dot? At 3 volts, the current is 0.5 amps. An amp is the unit of current. Now follow the line up. What do you think 6 volts gives?

1 amp, yes! Double the voltage, double the current. That straight line through the start is Ohm's law: current is proportional to voltage, as long as the temperature stays the same. What would 12 volts give?

2 amps, brilliant! Resistance tells you how hard it is for current to flow. Resistance equals voltage divided by current: 12 divided by 2 is 6 ohms. The ohm is the unit of resistance. Is the resistance the same at every point on this line?

Yes, 6 ohms everywhere, because the line is straight. Well done! Wow fact: a filament bulb does not obey Ohm's law; as it heats up its resistance grows, so its graph curves. Challenge: what current flows through a 10 ohm resistor on 5 volts?

faq.a: For a resistor at constant temperature, current is directly proportional to voltage. Double the voltage and the current doubles.
Resistance equals voltage divided by current. 12 volts with 2 amps gives 6 ohms.
Voltage, or potential difference, is the push that drives charge round a circuit. It is measured in volts.
Current is the rate of flow of electric charge, measured in amps.

faq.q: Why does a filament bulb not obey Ohm's law?
faq.a: As more current flows, the filament gets hotter and its resistance rises, so the current-voltage graph curves instead of staying straight.

facts: V = I × R: voltage (V) = current (A) × resistance (Ω).
A resistor at constant temperature gives a straight-line current–voltage graph through the origin.
